propositions.name: species_have_changed
propositions.statement: Species have changed and are still slowly changing by preservation and accumulation of slight favourable variations.
propositions.quote: species have changed, and are still slowly changing by the preservation and accumulation of successive slight favourable variations

propositions.name: descent_with_modification_general
propositions.statement: The theory of descent with modification embraces all members of the same class.
propositions.quote: I cannot doubt that the theory of descent with modification embraces all the members of the same class

propositions.name: common_parents_of_conspecifics
propositions.statement: All individuals of the same species and all species of the same genus must have descended from common parents.
propositions.quote: All the individuals of the same species, and all the species of the same genus, or even higher group, must have descended from common parents

propositions.name: natural_selection_acts_slowly
propositions.statement: Natural selection produces no sudden modification and acts only by very short and slow steps.
propositions.quote: natural selection acts solely by accumulating slight, successive, favourable variations, it can produce no great or sudden modification; it can act only by very short and slow steps

propositions.name: struggle_for_existence
propositions.statement: The struggle for existence inevitably follows from the high geometrical ratio of increase common to all organic beings.
propositions.quote: The struggle for existence inevitably follows from the high geometrical ratio of increase which is common to all organic beings

propositions.name: more_born_than_survive
propositions.statement: More individuals are born than can possibly survive, so slight differences determine which live and die.
propositions.quote: More individuals are born than can possibly survive. A grain in the balance will determine which individual shall live and which shall die

propositions.name: variability_under_nature
propositions.statement: Variability exists under nature, and natural selection must therefore act upon it.
propositions.quote: if there be any variability under nature, it would be an unaccountable fact if natural selection had not come into play

propositions.name: all_organs_variable
propositions.statement: All organs and instincts are variable in some slight degree.
propositions.quote: all organs and instincts are, in ever so slight a degree, variable

propositions.name: natura_non_facit_saltum
propositions.statement: Nature does not proceed by leaps but by graduated steps.
propositions.quote: the canon of "Natura non facit saltum," which every fresh addition to our knowledge tends to make more strictly correct

propositions.name: geological_record_imperfect
propositions.statement: The geological record is imperfect in an extreme degree, so its facts support descent with modification.
propositions.quote: If we admit that the geological record is imperfect in an extreme degree, then such facts as the record gives, support the theory of descent with modification

propositions.name: species_first_existed_as_varieties
propositions.statement: Species are strongly marked and permanent varieties; each species first existed as a variety.
propositions.quote: On the view that species are only strongly marked and permanent varieties, and that each species first existed as a variety

propositions.name: immutability_of_species_false
propositions.statement: The belief that species were immutable productions was unavoidable only under a short-duration view of the world.
propositions.quote: The belief that species were immutable productions was almost unavoidable as long as the history of the world was thought to be of short duration

propositions.name: extinction_from_natural_selection
propositions.statement: Extinction of species and whole groups almost inevitably follows from natural selection.
propositions.quote: The extinction of species and of whole groups of species, which has played so conspicuous a part in the history of the organic world, almost inevitably follows on the principle of natural selection

propositions.name: divergence_of_character
propositions.statement: Natural selection tends to preserve the most divergent offspring of any one species.
propositions.quote: there will be a constant tendency in natural selection to preserve the most divergent offspring of any one species

propositions.name: modifications_inheritable_long
propositions.statement: Modifications can be inherited for long periods.
propositions.quote: the amount has been large, and that modifications can be inherited for long periods

propositions.name: domestication_nature_analogy
propositions.statement: Principles that acted efficiently under domestication should also act under nature.
propositions.quote: There is no obvious reason why the principles which have acted so efficiently under domestication should not have acted under nature

propositions.name: lapse_of_time_immense
propositions.statement: The lapse of time is so great as to be utterly inappreciable by the human intellect.
propositions.quote: the lapse of time has been so great as to be utterly inappreciable by the human intellect

propositions.name: sterility_not_special_endowment
propositions.statement: Sterility of first crosses is incidental on constitutional differences in reproductive systems, not a special endowment.
propositions.quote: this sterility is no more a special endowment than is the incapacity of two trees to be grafted together, but that it is incidental on constitutional differences in the reproductive systems

propositions.name: natural_system_genealogical
propositions.statement: Affinities of organic beings are due to community of descent; the natural system is a genealogical arrangement.
propositions.quote: The real affinities of all organic beings are due to inheritance or community of descent. The natural system is a genealogical arrangement

propositions.name: homologous_pattern_from_progenitor
propositions.statement: Similarity of pattern across parts is intelligible as gradual modification of parts alike in a common early progenitor.
propositions.quote: is likewise intelligible on the view of the gradual modification of parts or organs, which were alike in the early progenitor of each class

propositions.name: embryo_resemblance_across_classes
propositions.statement: Embryos of mammals, birds, reptiles, and fishes closely resemble each other though the adults do not.
propositions.quote: we can clearly see why the embryos of mammals, birds, reptiles, and fishes should be so closely alike, and should be so unlike the adult forms

propositions.name: rudimentary_organs_show_progenitor
propositions.statement: Rudimentary organs plainly show that an early progenitor had the organ in a fully developed state.
propositions.quote: Organs in a rudimentary condition plainly show that an early progenitor had the organ in a fully developed state

propositions.name: descended_from_few_progenitors
propositions.statement: Animals have descended from at most four or five progenitors, and plants from an equal or lesser number.
propositions.quote: I believe that animals have descended from at most only four or five progenitors, and plants from an equal or lesser number

propositions.name: one_primordial_form
propositions.statement: Probably all organic beings that have lived on earth descended from one primordial form into which life was first breathed.
propositions.quote: probably all the organic beings which have ever lived on this earth have descended from some one primordial form, into which life was first breathed

propositions.name: no_species_variety_line
propositions.statement: No clear distinction has been or can be drawn between species and well-marked varieties.
propositions.quote: no clear distinction has been, or can be, drawn between species and well-marked varieties

propositions.name: correlation_of_growth
propositions.statement: Correlation of growth links modification of one part to modification of others.
propositions.quote: In both varieties and species correlation of growth seems to have played a most important part, so that when one part has been modified other parts are necessarily modified

propositions.name: use_and_disuse
propositions.statement: Use and disuse have produced some effect in both varieties and species.
propositions.quote: In both varieties and species, use and disuse seem to have produced some effect

propositions.name: mans_selection_produces_breeds
propositions.statement: Selection by man has been the great agency in producing the most distinct and useful domestic breeds.
propositions.quote: This process of selection has been the great agency in the production of the most distinct and useful domestic breeds

propositions.name: dominant_groups_beget_dominants
propositions.statement: Dominant species of larger groups tend to give birth to new and dominant forms, so each large group grows larger.
propositions.quote: Dominant species belonging to the larger groups tend to give birth to new and dominant forms; so that each large group tends to become still larger

propositions.name: intermediate_forms_exterminated
propositions.statement: Intermediate varieties are, in the long run, supplanted and exterminated.
propositions.quote: the intermediate varieties will, in the long run, be supplanted and exterminated

propositions.name: creation_inexplicable_for_grouping
propositions.statement: The grouping of all organic beings in subordinate groups is inexplicable on the theory of creation.
propositions.quote: This grand fact of the grouping of all organic beings seems to me utterly inexplicable on the theory of creation

propositions.name: reproductive_system_susceptible
propositions.statement: The reproductive system is eminently susceptible to changes in the conditions of life, causing variability.
propositions.quote: the reproductive system being eminently susceptible to changes in the conditions of life; so that this system, when not rendered impotent, fails to reproduce offspring exactly like the parent-form

propositions.name: geometrical_ratio_of_reproduction
propositions.statement: Each species tends by its geometrical ratio of reproduction to increase inordinately in number.
propositions.quote: each species tends by its geometrical ratio of reproduction to increase inordinately in number

propositions.name: secondary_causes_produce_species
propositions.statement: Production and extinction of species are due to secondary causes, like birth and death of the individual.
propositions.quote: the production and extinction of the past and present inhabitants of the world should have been due to secondary causes, like those determining the birth and death of the individual

propositions.name: migration_explains_distribution
propositions.statement: Descent with modification, combined with migration, explains most great leading facts in geographical distribution.
propositions.quote: then we can understand, on the theory of descent with modification, most of the great leading facts in Distribution
